analysis.one_liner: Creates local job guarantee pilots with guaranteed wages, federal-style health coverage, and paid leave.
analysis.headline: Senator Booker introduced the bill with two Democratic cosponsors, and it has sat in the Senate Finance Committee since referral with no further action.
analysis.plain_summary: The bill would create a three-year pilot program run by the Labor Department. It would award grants to local governments and Tribal entities in communities where unemployment is at least 1.5 times the national rate. Each grantee would guarantee a job to any adult resident who applies, at a wage no lower than the state minimum, the local prevailing wage, a union contract wage, or the federal minimum as if a pending minimum-wage bill (S. 2823) were law — whichever is highest — plus health coverage comparable to what federal employees get, paid family leave, and paid sick time. Grant money could also pay for child care, transportation, housing help, and job training, and the bill funds audits and a rigorous evaluation of the pilot's results.
analysis.who_benefits: Unemployed and underemployed adults in high-unemployment communities, including people with disabilities, people with criminal records reentering the workforce, and Tribal communities. Participants would get a guaranteed job paying at least the highest of several wage floors, federal-employee-style health coverage, paid family and sick leave, and supportive services like child care and transportation to keep them on the job. Up to 15 communities would be selected, with diversity required across urban, rural, and Tribal areas.

how_it_helps.text: Any adult 18 or older residing in a participating area who applies is guaranteed employment for the length of the pilot [S2].

Jobs must pay at least the greatest of the state or local minimum wage, the local prevailing wage for similar work, an applicable union contract wage, or the wage set by the Fair Labor Standards Act as if a separate minimum-wage bill (S. 2823) had been enacted [S2].
Participants must be covered by health insurance comparable to the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program, plus paid family leave and paid sick time [S2].

Grant funds may pay for supportive services — transportation, child care, dependent care, housing, and needs-related payments — plus job training, adult education and literacy, help for formerly incarcerated people reentering the workforce, and financial literacy activities [S2].
The bill bars grantees from using funds to replace or displace existing workers or undermine existing collective bargaining agreements, and covers program jobs under existing bargaining units [S2].

analysis.who_pays: Federal taxpayers. The bill appropriates 'such sums as may be necessary' into a new Job Guarantee Program Trust Fund, with no stated dollar cap, and also expands the Work Opportunity Tax Credit so employers get a tax credit for hiring program participants, an additional cost to the Treasury.

drawbacks.text: The appropriation is open-ended: the bill funds the program with 'such sums as may be necessary' rather than a fixed amount, so its total cost is unknown before enactment [S2].

It is only a pilot: grants end after three years and go to no more than 15 communities, so participants face a guaranteed job that is scheduled to disappear, and most high-unemployment areas get nothing [S2].

The wage floor is set by cross-reference to another bill (S. 2823) that has not passed, an untested drafting device that leaves the actual wage level dependent on the terms of separate legislation [S2].
Employers gain a new tax credit for hiring program graduates, which costs the Treasury and channels part of the program's benefit through employers [S2].

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: The pilot design limits the fiscal exposure: three years, 15 sites, required audits by the Labor Department's Inspector General, clawback of funds for misuse, and a required rigorous evaluation of effects on employment, poverty, health, and incarceration before any decision about expansion [S2]. The genuine weakness is the open-ended appropriation and the fact that participants' guaranteed jobs vanish when the pilot ends. On balance, the protections against displacing existing workers and the built-in evaluation make this a cautiously structured test rather than a full program.

outcome.mechanism: The bill was introduced and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, where it has not yet received a hearing, a markup, or a vote.

narrative.text: Senator Booker introduced the bill on February 12, 2026, joined by Senators Merkley and Warren [S1][S2][S3].
The Senate read it twice and referred it to the Committee on Finance the same day; that is the only action since [S4].

The bill text specifies the pilot's structure: grants to up to 15 eligible entities with unemployment at least 150 percent of the national rate, a three-year grant period, a Job Guarantee Program Trust Fund, and an Inspector General audit requirement [S2].

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: No outcome yet. Nothing has been decided beyond the initial referral, so high-unemployment communities have gained nothing, and no one has yet acted to advance or block the bill.

analysis.who_came_out_ahead_short: Too early to tell — bill sits in committee

industries.industry: Private employers in high-unemployment pilot areas
industries.note: A guaranteed public job with a high wage floor and benefits could pull workers out of low-wage private jobs and pressure local employers to raise pay, but the bill also gives employers a new tax credit for hiring program graduates and bars the program from displacing existing employees [S2].

industries.industry: Employers claiming the Work Opportunity Tax Credit
industries.note: The bill adds 'qualified participants in a job guarantee program' as a new category of workers who qualify for the existing federal hiring tax credit, giving employers a subsidy for hiring people after three months in the program [S2].

industries.industry: Public workforce boards, training providers, and child care services
industries.note: Grant funds flow to supportive services, training, adult education, and child care, much of it delivered through the existing public workforce system, creating funded work for these providers [S2].

analysis.trajectory: With no Republican cosponsors, referral to the Finance Committee, and no hearing scheduled, the bill's most likely path is to sit in committee for the rest of the Congress. Its realistic best outcome would be having pieces folded into a larger economic or infrastructure package, if one moves.
